channel.description: Get the latest technology news, AI developments, startup funding updates, business enterprise and IT industry insights, cybersecurity alerts, and digital policy trends from India and around the world on ET Tech

item.title: Qualcomm to cut jobs worldwide in performance-focused layoffs, internal memo shows
item.description: The cuts are part of an effort to build "a stronger performance culture" and address situations where the company "has consistently fallen short of expectations," Amon said.

item.title: Ahead of massive IPOs, AI companies are sketching plans to share their wealth
item.description: On Sunday, Anthropic said it would commit 5% of its shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new entity within the company, pending approval from stockholders. The stake could increase "as the company grows" in the future. The maker of AI assistant Claude said the fund "might explore" larger donations to traditional nonprofits or potentially distribute money to "specific populations."

item.title: Anthropic recorded net loss of over $80 billion in first half of this year
item.description: AI startup Anthropic recorded a net loss of more than $80 billion in the first half of this year, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday.

item.title: Netflix issues weak fourth-quarter forecast, shares drop
item.description: Third-quarter revenue rose 11.8% to $12.87 billion, in line with Wall Street forecasts, but the lowest rate of increase in nearly three years. The company forecast fourth-quarter net income of $2.79 billion and EPS of 67 cents, below the average analyst forecast of $3.07 billion and 73 cents.

item.title: US banning Chinese AI DeepSeek from government agency IT systems
item.description: The department is also banning acquisition of DeepSeek products and third-party services developed using DeepSeek by US civilian government agencies. DHS said DeepSeek models pose "multiple threat vectors" and raised concerns that use of the product "may result in the transfer of sensitive data to the PRC if used by US government employees or vendors."

item.title: Netflix film division boss to exit in second senior departure in a week
item.description: Netflix said on Monday its film division head Dan Lin would leave after nearly three years at the helm, marking a second senior executive departure in less than a week amid concerns

item.title: Ex-OpenAI employee accused of planting device appears to have Saudi backing: court filing
item.description: US prosecutors allege that the defendant, Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, was in frequent communication with an unnamed member of the Saudi Royal family and that a member of the Saudi military paid for a one-way plane ticket for Alfozan's wife and son to return to Saudi Arabia, according to the court document.

item.title: Apple to host 'Pro and tell' event on October 28 in LA
item.description: Apple said on Monday it would host a "Pro and tell" event in Los Angeles on October 28, the latest in a series of product launches as the iPhone maker expands its hardware lineup and AI offerings.

item.title: Rapido says man linked to Tiger Shroff shooting incident was not an active captain
item.description: Shroff, who was reportedly the target of the attack, escaped unhurt. In a statement posted on social media, Rapido said it was “deeply concerned” by the incident involving the actor and his team and was relieved that he was safe. It also wished him a swift recovery.

item.title: Nvidia wins fast-growing AI startup Modal for new central processors
item.description: Modal, a cloud-computing startup that rents out computing power to AI developers, said it plans to start using Nvidia's new Vera central processor for the first time for hosting agents, the AI systems that can carry out long-running tasks for human users. Modal until now has run such work only on Intel and AMD chips.

item.title: Zetwerk IPO fully subscribed; Super.money triples revenues
item.description: Zetwerk’s Rs 5,012-crore IPO was subscribed 3.06 times on Monday, the last day for bids. This and more in today’s ETtech Top 5.

item.title: Lab-grown diamond startup So/Facet raises Rs 10 crore led by Sauce
item.description: The round also saw participation from Mokobara cofounders Sangeet Agrawal and Navin Parwal, Chona Family Office (that’s behind Hocco Ice Creams), Haleon South Asia president Kedar Lele, and Moonshot co-founder Devaiah Bopanna.

item.title: Auto tech companies raise $1.3 billion in 2026 so far: Tracxn
item.description: The funding rounds were led by ride-hailing firm Rapido's $240 million, followed by electric two-wheeler manufacturer Simple Energy's $180 million and River's $102 million.

item.title: Netflix faces questions on user engagement ahead of third-quarter report
item.description: Ted Sarandos, the co-CEO of Netflix, recently admitted the company "is not growing as fast as I want us to", and suggested live programming could be an opportunity to accelerate growth.

item.title: ISB programme explores AI’s growing role in the future of digital finance
item.description: The Executive Programme in Fintech and AI at ISB is crafted to equip finance professionals with cutting-edge skills in financial services. Spanning 32 weeks, this program offers live online sessions alongside engaging experiential learning. Participants will delve into real-world applications of fintech, artificial intelligence, and blockchain. Tailored for senior finance leaders, this course seeks to enhance strategic decision-making. Applications for the next cohort are now open, creating valuable networking opportunities.

item.title: Govt asks Meta to ensure its recommendation systems do not expose users to a limited set of narratives
item.description: The advisory by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), dated October 10, asked Meta to undertake appropriate measures to provide adequate context in relation to photographs, videos, graphics, or other content depicting ongoing public events, particularly where the authenticity, date, location or circumstances of such content may not be readily apparent to users.

item.title: VC’s remark on deeptech sets off a debate on where India’s capital should go
item.description: “In a decade we will realize most of the deeptech is a grift,” Maini wrote, adding that quick services and quick commerce companies will do more to drive the economy. The remark, a reply to a post by Neosapien CEO Dhananjay Yadav, drew heavy reactions on X.

item.title: Samsung to use TSMC technology for Nvidia's next-generation memory chips: Report
item.description: Nvidia has asked Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron Technology to use TSMC's process for NVHBM base dies, and sixth-generation DRAM technology for its core dies, the newspaper said, citing industry sources.

item.title: Only 8% of fund managers report improved investment returns from AI adoption: Report
item.description: Despite growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in the global asset management industry, only 8 per cent of fund managers have reported measurable improvements in investment returns, according to a joint research report by Morgan Stanley and Oliver Wyman.

item.title: Accenture looks to sell Chinese operations for up to $1.5 billion: FT
item.description: IT consulting firm Accenture is looking to sell its Chinese operations for up to $1.5 billion, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

item.title: Microsoft pulls out of UK data center deal with Nscale: Telegraph
item.description: The US tech giant, one of Nscale's two largest customers, recently terminated its agreement for the data center in Loughton, Essex, according to the report.

item.title: ‘Dad, the internet at home is too slow’: How Jio’s founding idea took shape
item.description: Isha Ambani's concerns regarding poor household internet sparked important conversations about India's digital landscape, leading to transformative innovations. In response, Mukesh Ambani pioneered Reliance Jio in 2011, aiming to enhance mobile connectivity across the nation. Its launch in September 2016 revolutionized the telecom sector by offering affordable data and complimentary voice services.

item.title: AI bubble burst may trigger 2008-like banking crisis, says Gary Marcus
item.description: In a recent discussion, Gary Marcus raised critical flags about OpenAI's fiscal responsibilities as the stock market faces instability. He warned that the demise of leading AI firms could trigger extensive financial repercussions. Notably, Marcus compared the current climate to WeWork's disastrous decline, suggesting that Microsoft might pick up OpenAI at a bargain.

item.title: From shareholders to partners: How Google and Meta’s Jio investments evolved into an AI alliance
item.description: Meta and Google, originally minority shareholders in Jio Platforms, are now forming strategic partnerships with Reliance. The new collaborations focus on enterprise AI initiatives and dedicated cloud infrastructure in India. Meta's joint venture will leverage Llama models for developing AI platforms, while Google focuses on establishing cloud services. Both companies aim to enhance Reliance's capabilities in AI and cloud technology sectors.

item.title: Microsoft president warns Trump's H-1B, green card crackdown could drive tech talent out of US
item.description: Speaking with POLITICO on the sidelines of the International AI Summit in Dublin, Ireland, Smith raised concerns over the administration's move to restrict permanent residency applications for skilled foreign employees at Microsoft and seven other companies.

item.title: Meta employees said Lula's accounts were hindered during Brazil election: Report
item.description: The messages also acknowledged that the platform recommended the profile of challenger Flavio Bolsonaro, as well as his WhatsApp channel, according to the report.

item.title: CoreWeave's CEO sold nearly $1 billion of stock since IPO, filings show
item.description: The sales began about two months after the stock hit a record high in June 2025. The shares have tumbled since and were on track to lose about 24% this week as investors worried about the Nvidia-backed company's heavy capital spending and the debt needed to fund it amid rising bets on interest-rate hikes.

item.title: ETtech Deals Digest: Boldfit, GreenCell lead as weekly funding hits $232 million, down 45% on-year
item.description: Boldfit led deal activity with $41.5 million, followed by GreenCell Mobility at $34.5 million, Inner Sky Labs at $30.9 million, and Scimplify at $25 million. Accel was among the most active investors, backing Scimplify, Origin, and CosmoChute. Elevation Capital invested in Mesa School of Business and Spill Games, while Pantera Capital backed Fission Labs.

item.title: Urban Company announces plans to enter residential air conditioner segment
item.description: Urban Company currently sells water purifiers and smart locks under the Native brand. ET had first reported in October 2025 about the company exploring its foray in this space. With this Urban Company will join a list of new-age firms to sell air conditioners - a market that is currently dominated by legacy brands such as Samsung, Daikin, Godrej and Voltas.

item.title: LTM profit dips marginally, revenue up 13.6% YoY
item.description: Revenue recorded healthy growth on a year-on-year (YoY) basis by 13.6% to Rs 11,807.6 crore supported by financial services, consumer and production sector in key regions of North America and Europe. Rest of the World region and technology & services vertical showed a sequential degrowth, which impacted revenue to grow by 1.7% from the June quarter.

item.title: Supermarket operator Ahold's websites, app remain offline 5 days after cyber incident
item.description: An Ahold spokesperson said the parent company cannot comment about the situation at its individual chains. Its US brands, which include Stop & Shop, Giant Food, Hannaford and Food Lion, are collectively one of the largest food retailers in the United States. Physical stores remain open.

item.title: What is Meta’s Muse Spark Open and what can it do?
item.description: An open-weight model is an AI model whose core components — the numerical parameters learned during its training, known as its weights — are released publicly. Anyone can download the model, run it on their computer, study how it works, and adapt it to their needs, subject to the model’s licence and usage terms.

item.title: Urban Company Q2 Results: Loss widens to Rs 182 crore; revenue jumps 41% YoY
item.description: Urban Company reported a net loss of Rs 182 crore in Q2FY27 as investments in its quick services business, InstaHelp, weighed on profitability. Revenue rose 41% year-on-year to Rs 537 crore, while orders grew 103%. The company also approved a fresh capital raise of up to Rs 2,500 crore, subject to shareholder approval.

item.title: Urban Company board approves plan to raise Rs 2,500 crore via QIP
item.description: In a letter to shareholders, the Gurugram-based company said it had Rs 1,901 crore in cash as of September 30, while its businesses excluding the InstaHelp segment generated Rs 119 crore in adjusted Ebitda over the past nine months.

item.title: Anthropic cofounder renews call for robust regulation of frontier AI
item.description: Concerns about AI guardrails have soared after models developed by OpenAI and Anthropic were involved in security incidents during testing, piling on pressure to regulate the technology.

item.title: Ather Energy gets Irdai licence, will distribute and service insurance policies
item.description: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India granted the subsidiary a certificate of registration on October 15 to act as a corporate agent (composite), Ather Energy said in a stock exchange filing on Thursday. The registration covers life, general and health insurance.

item.title: Anthropic's Jack Clark says common-sense standards are needed for AI
item.description: Anthropic tests its AI systems and shares that information, but it should not all be voluntary, Clark added during a panel discussion at the IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok.

item.title: Low-cost jobs will be taken over by AI, most worried about outsourced ones: Workday CEO
item.description: Workday Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Aneel Bhusri told reporters at the Workday Rising Summit that AI will not lead to jobs moving out of the US or first-world countries, but may do the opposite.

item.title: How GoDaddy is changing the way Indian SMBs use AI
item.description: Online presence for enterprises have become vital, and thankfully with the advent of AI, easier as well. While creating a website, branding, logos, and finding the right potential customers was a matter of expertise in yesteryears, it can now be done without having the relevant skills and/or resources. GoDaddy, as always, is leading the way!

item.title: New York City pension fund asks Anthropic to delay IPO
item.description: The supervisor of New York City's pension funds, one of the largest in the United States, asked Anthropic to postpone its stock market debut until risks posed by its artificial intelligence technology are better controlled. A small fraction of those assets, around $7 million, are currently exposed to Anthropic, the Comptroller's office told AFP. However, that exposure will grow if Anthropic goes public because its shares would become included in several stock indices, including the Russell 3000, which New York City tracks for its own investments.

item.title: 'Mixed feelings': AI cracks centuries-old ciphers
item.description: Napoleon Bonaparte ordered the wartime missive written in code, creating a puzzle that went unsolved for more than 200 years -- until AI cracked it in a matter of hours. Tomokiyo said that since mid-September, most of the ciphers on his list have been cracked using AI. "There remain some tough problems" which could stay an enigma for years to come, because there is less relevant data available to help AI figure them out, the 58-year-old told AFP. "I'm excited long-time problems are now solved, but on the other hand, I have mixed feelings, because AI seems to have solved these difficult problems so easily," he said.

item.title: Google boosts news and link visibility in AI mode
item.description: Google announced Thursday it will start displaying links to websites and articles more prominently and higher up in search results powered by artificial intelligence (AI), as brands and news publishers warn of a sharp decline in their traffic. According to a report by consultancy Chartbeat, news website publishers saw a 40 percent drop in traffic coming from Google between July 2025 and July 2026.

item.title: Google warns suspected China-linked hackers could exploit BeyondTrust flaw
item.description: Google warned on Thursday that organizations should prepare for "potential widespread exploitation" after a new bug was found in US cybersecurity firm BeyondTrust's remote support appliances.

item.title: Meta releases open-weight Muse Spark model for coding, agentic tasks
item.description: Open-weight models make trained parameters available for developers to modify, unlike proprietary models that remain under their creators' control. They can offer businesses a lower-cost alternative to closed systems.

item.title: Investors temper Anthropic IPO valuation expectations over revenue growth slowdown
item.description: Some investors who attended Anthropic's investor day on Wednesday in San Francisco discussed a valuation of around $1.5 trillion, three of the people said, a significant step down from the roughly $2 trillion valuation that investors had previously expected for the November share sale.

item.title: Flipkart ex-staff push for Esop buyout; Wipro, Tech Mahindra’s Q2 report
item.description: Happy Friday! Former Flipkart employees are asking Walmart to cash out their vested stock options. This and more in today’s ETtech Morning Dispatch.

item.title: Nvidia, Apple each gave $25 million for Trump's ballroom: Washington Post
item.description: The Adelson family, longtime financial supporters of Trump and his Republican Party, committed $25 million as well, as did billionaire Charles Ergen, co-founder and chairman of telecommunications company Dish Network, the report added.

item.title: Amazon launches two new portable AI listening devices
item.description: Frontier is a bracelet and Eclipse is a brick that resembles a portable magnetic charger. Users attach the devices to their smartphones. They aggregate information from calendars, apps like email and other points throughout the day that are accessed through an app or a website, Amazon said.

item.title: CNN signs multi-year AI partnership with Google
item.description: The deal marks the first partnership announced since Skydance's merger with Paramount, under CEO David Ellison, who has sought to position the media group as a technology-driven business.

item.title: CoreWeave's slump puts spotlight on debt behind AI boom
item.description: The loss-making AI cloud company, burdened with about $50 billion in debt, has become the poster child for mounting concerns that the data center boom is being fueled by credit, straining newer players and pressuring cash flows even at giants such as Alphabet and Meta Platforms.
